newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco targets Queensland for smelter.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco targets Queensland for smelter.

text.p: Bauxite miner and alumina producer Comalco Ltd said on Wednesday that Queensland was the preferred location for its planned A$1 billion alumina refinery.
"In principle, Queensland is a preferred location provided the relative economies are in place," Comalco Minerals & Alumina (CM&A) managing director Rod Kinkead-Weekes told a news conference.
Kinkead-Weekes said he stressed talks were also going on with the Malaysian Government on a possible refinery site but no decision had been taken on either of the alternatives.
Comalco was still discussing electricity charges for the new refinery with the Queensland Government, Kinkead-Weekes said.
A decision on the new refinery site was expected in the next two to three months, he said.
"Having done that, we need to do engineering studies on a site-specific location. That's a process that could take several months," he said.
Kinkead-Weekes said the earlier-announced closure of Comalco's kaolin operations at Weipa in far north Queensland was also aimed at reducing costs to a minimum ahead of the refinery start-up date.
The kaolin operations represented a significant investment of nearly A$80 million over 10 years -- "we had better use for the money", he said.
Kinkead-Weekes said production assets of the kaolin project were for sale but the kaolin deposit would remain on a care and maintenance basis indefinitely.
